submitted.rationale: Index 4 (Sb 0.32, Zn 0.68) had the highest EQE of the three measurements: 0.195%. It sits between the Zn7Sb2O12 spinel and ZnSb2O6 trirutile compositions, so it is probably a spinel-rich two-phase mixture. The foundation models predict that both phases are stable or nearly stable and absorb at 3.2 eV (MEGNet gaps about 2 eV).

rejected.reason: Near phase-pure ZnSb2O6 trirutile, on the hull; measured EQE 0.070%, the lowest of the three.
Near phase-pure Zn7Sb2O12 spinel; measured EQE 0.114%, below the mixed-phase index 4.
Not measured because the merit budget ran out; EQE trended downward toward the Sb-rich trirutile side.

consultations.verdict: Support: trirutile ZnSb2O6 (mp-3188) is on the MACE hull (0 eV/atom) and MEGNet HSE gap 1.97 eV < 3.2 eV photon energy, so a phase-pure ZnSb2O6 composition (Sb~0.67, index 16) should absorb and be a stable photoanode candidate.

Support (moderate): Zn7Sb2O12 spinel (mp-675797) is near-hull by MACE (0.012 eV/atom) and MEGNet gap ~1.95 eV < 3.2 eV, so it should absorb. It is a distinct phase from the trirutile measured at index 16 (0.07% EQE), so it is the most informative contrast; index 1 (Sb 0.243) is closest to its 0.222 stoichiometry.

Support (weak): the second spinel Zn7Sb2O12 polymorph (mp-1215862) has a MEGNet gap of 2.08 eV, so it absorbs at 3.2 eV. The Zn-rich spinel side gave the higher EQE (0.114% vs 0.070%). Index 4 (Sb 0.32) is spinel-rich with some trirutile and has the highest GP mean among unmeasured points, so it tests whether a two-phase heterojunction beats phase-pure spinel.
